scheme_name: "Integrated Farming for Productivity Improvement Scheme" by the Coconut Development Board
description:
The Integrated Farming for Productivity Improvement Scheme is a significant initiative launched by the Coconut Development Board in India. 

This scheme was officially launched in the year 2019. 

It aims to enhance the productivity and profitability of coconut farming through an integrated approach. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to promote sustainable farming practices. 

It focuses on improving the overall productivity of coconut farms by integrating various agricultural practices. 

The scheme is designed to benefit coconut farmers across the country. 

One of the measurable targets is to increase coconut productivity from the current average of 8,000 nuts per hectare to 12,000 nuts per hectare by the year 2025. 

The scheme also aims to enhance the income of farmers by at least 30 percent within the next five years. 

Under this scheme, farmers are provided with financial assistance to adopt modern farming techniques. 

The Coconut Development Board allocates a budget of approximately ₹100 crores annually for this scheme. 

Farmers can receive a subsidy of up to 50 percent on the cost of inputs and equipment. 

The maximum financial assistance provided to each farmer under this scheme can go up to ₹1 lakh. 

This assistance is aimed at promoting the use of high-yielding coconut varieties and advanced agricultural practices. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of intercropping and diversification. 

Farmers are encouraged to cultivate compatible crops alongside coconut trees. 

This practice not only increases the overall yield but also improves soil health. 

Eligible crops for intercropping include black pepper, vanilla, and turmeric. 

The Coconut Development Board also provides training and capacity-building programs for farmers. 

These programs are designed to educate farmers about best practices in coconut cultivation. 

The training sessions cover topics such as pest management, soil health, and water conservation techniques. 

To be eligible for the scheme, farmers must own a minimum of 0.5 hectares of coconut land. 

There is no upper limit on the size of land that can be covered under this scheme. 

Farmers must also be registered with the Coconut Development Board to avail of the benefits. 

The income limit for eligibility is set at ₹2 lakh per annum for small and marginal farmers. 

For larger farmers, the income limit is ₹5 lakh per annum. 

The application process for the scheme is straightforward. 

Farmers need to fill out an application form available at the local Coconut Development Board office. 

Required documents include proof of land ownership, identity proof, and income certificate. 

Farmers must also submit a project proposal outlining their intended activities under the scheme. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the local Coconut Development Board officials. 

The approval process typically takes about 30 days. 

After approval, the financial assistance is disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account. 

Disbursement is usually done in two installments. 

The first installment is released upon approval of the project. 

The second installment is released after the successful implementation of the project. 

The scheme is implemented by the Coconut Development Board at the national level. 

The Board operates under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The contact details for the Coconut Development Board can be found on their official website. 

Farmers can also reach out to local offices for assistance and guidance. 

The scheme has shown promising results in states like Kerala and Tamil Nadu. 

In Kerala, the productivity of coconut has increased by 20 percent since the launch of the scheme. 

In Tamil Nadu, farmers have reported an increase in income by approximately ₹30,000 per year. 

The scheme also aims to promote organic farming practices among coconut farmers. 

Farmers are encouraged to use organic fertilizers and pesticides. 

This shift towards organic farming is expected to improve the quality of coconut products. 

The Coconut Development Board also collaborates with research institutions. 

These collaborations aim to develop new coconut varieties that are more resilient to climate change. 

The scheme has a special focus on women farmers. 

Women are encouraged to participate in training programs and workshops. 

The Board aims to empower women by providing them with skills and knowledge. 

The Integrated Farming for Productivity Improvement Scheme is part of a larger strategy. 

This strategy aims to make coconut farming more sustainable and profitable. 

The scheme aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The Coconut Development Board regularly monitors the progress of the scheme. 

Feedback from farmers is collected to improve the implementation process. 

The scheme also promotes the use of technology in farming. 

Farmers are encouraged to use mobile applications for pest management and weather updates. 

The integration of technology is expected to enhance decision-making for farmers. 

Overall, the Integrated Farming for Productivity Improvement Scheme is a comprehensive initiative. 

It addresses multiple aspects of coconut farming to ensure better productivity and income for farmers. 

The scheme is expected to play a crucial role in the development of the coconut sector in India. 

With the right support and implementation, it has the potential to transform the livelihoods of coconut farmers across the country. 

The Coconut Development Board continues to work towards achieving the objectives set forth in this scheme. 

The focus remains on sustainable practices and improving the economic conditions of farmers. 

This initiative is a testament to the government's commitment to agricultural development. 

The Integrated Farming for Productivity Improvement Scheme is a vital step towards achieving food security and enhancing rural livelihoods in India.
